words.explanation: vi. to jump into the water with your head and arms going in first 跳水
words.example: The warm-up is a must before you dive into the pool.

words.explanation: vt. to continue doing an activity or trying to achieve sth. over a long period of time 追求；继续；从事
words.example: Mary hopes to pursue a career in medicine after college.

words.explanation: n. [C] 1 sth. you have to do that is very boring or difficult（必须做的）乏味无聊的事务；困难的工作
words.example: Cleaning out the kitchen is a real chore.

words.explanation: vi. ( ~ with ) to succeed in dealing with a difficult problem or job（成功地）应付，对付
words.example: She feared she wouldn't be able to cope with the study in college.

words.explanation: vt. to say that sth. is not true, or that you do not believe sth. 否认；否定
words.example: You can't deny the fact that practice makes perfect.

words.explanation: n. [U] the state or quality of being complicated and detailed 复杂性；错综复杂
words.example: The elderly struggle with the complexity of digital payment.

words.explanation: a. serious, important, or useful 严肃的；重要的；有用的
words.example: Life is not meaningful without work.

words.explanation: v. to gradually change your behavior and ideas to fit a new situation（使）适应；（使）适合
words.example: Her children adapted quickly to living in a small village.

words.explanation: n. [C] ( infml. ) 宿舍
vi. to regularly travel a long distance to get to work（经常）经很远的路程上/下班
words.example: Mary commutes from home to campus every day.

words.explanation: n. [U] 成年（时期）
words.example: Changing from youth to adulthood can be very painful.

words.explanation: n. [C] ( fml. ) 兄弟；姊妹
n. [C] sth. that unites two or more people or groups, such as love, or a shared interest or idea 纽带；联结；联系；关系
words.example: After these troubles, the bond between my parents and me gets stronger.

words.explanation: n. [C, usu. sing.] the period of time during which sb. is alive or sth. exists 一生；终生
words.example: Youth comes only once in a lifetime.

words.explanation: a. relating to feelings of love or a loving relationship 浪漫的；风流的
words.example: She wishes her boyfriend could be a bit more romantic.

words.explanation: n. [C, U] 1 sth. that makes you want to have or do sth., even though you know you should not 很有诱惑力的事物
words.example: The cake on the desk was too strong a temptation for kids to resist.

words.explanation: n. [C] a plan of what sb. is going to do and when they are going to do it 计划表；进度表；日程表
words.example: The next thing on our schedule is to visit our friends.

words.explanation: a. always complaining 一味抱怨的
words.example: His nagging wife is always complaining about small things.

words.explanation: n. [C] a way of thinking about sth., which is influenced by the kind of person you are or by your experiences（思考问题的）角度；观点；想法
words.example: The story is told from the perspective of an ordinary farmer.

words.explanation: a. 1 always trying to be more successful than other people 有竞争意识的；好竞争的
words.example: Bella is so competitive, even with her parents and friends.

words.explanation: a. not honest 不老实的；不诚实的
words.example: The dishonest manager was fired by the company.

words.explanation: n. [U] the money or other benefits that you can get from sth. 利润；收益；利益
words.example: He seems to have entered the organization only for personal gain.

words.explanation: n. [C] ( be on the ~ for sth. ) to continuously watch a place or pay attention in order to find sth. you want or to be ready for problems or opportunities 监视某事物；留神观察某事物
words.example: You've got to be on the lookout for thieves when you get on a bus.

words.explanation: a. caring only about yourself and not about other people 自私的；自私自利的
words.example: She never considers anyone but herself – she's totally selfsh.

words.explanation: n. 1 [U] a medical condition that makes you feel extremely unhappy, so that you cannot live a normal life 抑郁症
words.example: Many Americans suﬀer from depression at some point in their lives.

words.explanation: vt. to make an illness or an injury better, usu. by medical treatment 治疗，治好（伤病）
words.example: Doctors won't consider him cured until he has been free of cancer for several years.

words.example: Keep a dictionary handy when you preview the text.

words.explanation: n. [C] 治疗专家
vi. ( fml. ) to become very successful or very strong and healthy 兴旺；欣欣向荣；茁壮成长
words.example: I wouldn't want that much pressure, but my brother seems to thrive on it.

words.explanation: to quickly become completely involved in an activity, a subject, etc. 全身心地投入；潜心钻研
words.example: He was eager to dive into the kind of opportunities the college oﬀers.

words.explanation: ( infml. ) to spend a lot of time in a particular place or with particular people 长时间呆在某地；和某人长时间呆在一起
words.example: I am not going to hang out with him anymore because he is always late.

words.explanation: ( spoken ) used to say that it is very clear that sth. is true 无可否认；不容否认
words.example: There's no denying that parents are the best teachers for their children.

words.explanation: without having a good reason or purpose 平白无故地；白白地
words.example: We walked all the way down there for nothing.

words.explanation: to not speak or write to sb. anymore, because they do not live near you, work with you, etc. 失去联系
words.example: Call me as soon as you can. I don't want to lose touch with you.

words.explanation: to spend time with sb. 与（某人）在一起
words.example: Parents warned the kids not to associate with bad friends.

words.explanation: to do sth. so that you can be certain of the result 设法确保
words.example: We should set out early if we want to make sure of getting there on time.

words.explanation: to believe that sth. is worth paying attention to or should be respected 认真对待某事
words.example: Scientists have begun to take the risk of depression in children seriously.
